Title: Co‑sell technical storyboard and deal architecture guide
Space: sales-enablement

Summary
========
This playbook equips account teams and solutions engineers for co‑sell motions with systems integrators (SIs), ISVs, and strategic channel partners. It codifies an end‑to‑end technical storyboard, a competitive brief, recommended pitch deck flow, pragmatic pricing guidance for pilots → reserved capacity → enterprise, a short anonymized case example, a security quick‑reference for prospects, and objection handling tailored to co‑selling scenarios.

Why this doc exists
--------------------
- Co‑sell opportunities require a single technical narrative that both Redwood and the partner can reuse in demos and proposals.
- Sales conversations escalate faster when commercial and technical asks are synchronized (pilot scope, prognosed costs, data residency needs).
- Provide reproducible artifacts (diagram text, config table, Q&A) to reduce SE prep time and avoid misalignment.

Intended audience
------------------
- Account executives and solution architects
- Partner SDRs and technical alliance managers
- Pre‑sales engineers and partner SEs

Target buyer personas
---------------------
- Platform/AI Product Lead (mid‑market/enterprise) — cares about cost per inference, latency, and dev ergonomics
- Infrastructure/Cloud Architect — cares about VPC, KMS, on‑prem packaging, and network egress
- Compliance Officer — cares about audit logs, data residency, and contractual SLAs

Core positioning pillars (co‑sell framing)
-----------------------------------------
1) Predictable economics at scale
   - Demonstrate unit economics (tokens/embedding) and the path from pilot cost to 40–60% cost reduction via Dedicated + batching + KV cache.
2) One API, all deployment modes
   - Sell the narrative: same API/ops experience from hosted → dedicated → private VPC; reduces integration risk.
3) Production reliability and fallbacks
   - Emphasize routing policies, automatic fallback models, and per‑route observability to meet availability targets.

Technical storyboard (script for demos and technical discovery)
----------------------------------------------------------------
1) Discovery and constraints (5–10 min)
   - Confirm: peak qps, average request size (tokens), tail latency targets (P95 ≤ 300ms), data residency requirement, encryption-at-rest key provider (KMS/HSM).
   - Capture: integration pattern (direct API vs. private endpoint vs. on‑prem), expected concurrent users, and retention of input logs.

2) Demo narrative (10–15 min)
   - Step 1: Hosted API quickstart — show <curl> generation and streaming response.
   - Step 2: Activation of a Dedicated pool — illustrate predictable throughput numbers for a 4×A100 equivalent pool (example throughput: ~5000 prompt tokens/s, depends on model/seq length).
   - Step 3: Fallback demonstration — intentionally degrade primary model and show automatic routing to a lower‑cost compatible variant without changing the client code.

3) Integration diagram (to include in proposals)
   - ASCII diagram to paste into proposals:

       Client App → (TLS) → Redwood Gateway (API) → Router
          ├─ Hosted Cluster (public)
          ├─ Dedicated Pool (customer‑reserved)
          └─ Private VPC Connector → Customer VPC / On‑prem Runtime

   - Callouts: show where KMS integrates (private), where audit logs are exported (SIEM), and where prefix caching occurs.

4) Pilot checklist (technical acceptance criteria)
   - Ingress/egress tested (throughput and TLS termination)
   - Latency SLO validated against synthetic traffic (P50, P95)
   - Cost projection agreed (sample 7‑day usage extrapolated to monthly)
   - Security review (KMS, SOC2 artifacts, contractual confidentiality)

Competitive brief (concise, for partner enablement)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Primary competitors to call out: large cloud hosted LLM endpoints, inference‑only vendors, and vendor B offering self‑hosted runtime.
- Quick differentiators to use in conversation:
  - Runtime + orchestration: Redwood couples a GPU‑optimized runtime with smart routing and automatic fallbacks (vs. pure endpoint providers).
  - Unified operations: same API and rollout primitives across hosted/dedicated/private (vs. fragmented offerings requiring custom glue).
  - Cost controls: first‑class batching, KV prefix caching, and quantization profiles with recommended savings estimates.

Battlecard snippets
-------------------
- Objection: “We can run this ourselves on cloud VMs”
  - Reply: Upfront engineering cost to achieve equivalent throughput, and lack of a unified rollout/observability layer increases time to recover from regressions. Redwood reduces operational burden and accelerates time to value.
- Objection: “We need on‑prem”
  - Reply: Redwood Private supports VPC and on‑prem packaging with KMS/HSM integration and audit logging; we run a joint integration plan with partner SIs.

Pricing guidance (pilot → enterprise)
------------------------------------
- Pilot (0–90 days)
  - Objective: validate UAT traffic pattern and ROI signals. Offer a time‑boxed credit or discounted hosted tier (e.g., 50% off hosted token price up to $20K usage) and a short‑term Dedicated trial (2‑4 weeks of reserved capacity at a fixed rate).
- Scale path (committed Dedicated)
  - Example structure: commit to N GPU‑equivalent capacity (monthly SKU) + overage at a discounted per‑token rate. Typical anchor: $25K–$150K/month depending on throughput and retention.
- Enterprise (Private + SLAs)
  - Platform fee (one‑time onboarding) + annual support + consumption or reserved capacity. Include optional add‑ons: extended observability retention, compliance attestation package.

Pricing worksheet example (paste into proposal)
-----------------------------------------------
| Item | Quantity | Unit | Monthly | Notes |
| Pilot hosted credit | 1 | $ | $0 (credit) | Time‑boxed up to $20K usage |
| Dedicated reserve | 1 | gpu‑equiv | $45,000 | Example 4×A100 equivalent pool |
| Onboarding professional services | 1 | one‑time | $30,000 | SI integration and runbook codification |

Case study vignette (anonymized)
--------------------------------
- Customer: Global e‑commerce platform (anonymized)
- Challenge: Answer personalization features with sub‑300ms P95 across EU traffic, cost blowout in proof‑of‑concept.
- Outcome: Pilot used Hosted API for 3 weeks, migrated to Dedicated with prefix caching and quantization recommendations. Resulted in 47% per‑query cost reduction and stable P95 ≈ 260ms. Went into enterprise contract for Dedicated + Private in EU region.

Security quick‑reference for prospects (top Qs and one‑line answers)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Q: How is customer data isolated in Dedicated and Private deployments?
A: Dedicated uses isolated GPU pools and data namespaces; Private runs inside customer VPC or on‑prem with customer network controls.

Q: Do you support customer KMS/HSM for key management?
A: Yes — Redwood integrates with cloud KMS providers and HSMs for Private deployments; we document key rotation and access patterns in the integration plan.

Q: What audit evidence can you provide?
A: SOC2 Type II report, audit logging schema (JSON lines), per‑token usage logs with hash‑pseudonymization options; sample artifacts provided under NDA.

Q: How do you handle egress and data residency?
A: Region‑bounded deployments, private connectors, and contractual commitments for data residency. On‑prem option eliminates egress concerns.

Q: What is the remediation plan for model quality regressions?
A: Canary rollouts, automatic fallback to vetted variants, and prompt/eval hooks that trigger a regression alert to SRE and the customer success team.

Partner onboarding checklist (for SIs)
-------------------------------------
1) Complete technical enablement: runtime fundamentals, routing policies, and API quickstarts.
2) Joint demo rehearsals with AE and partner SE.
3) Agree on pilot KPIs and acceptance criteria.
4) Exchange contact tree and escalation matrix.

Pitch deck recommended slide flow (15 slides)
---------------------------------------------
1) Title / value headline
2) Customer problem and metrics
3) Redwood short positioning (one‑liner + stats)
4) Architecture: integration options
5) Technical storyboard snapshot (ASCII diagram)
6) Performance snapshot (P95 targets, throughput examples)
7) Cost comparison (pilot vs Dedicated)
8) Security & compliance highlights
9) Case vignette
10) Deployment & timeline
11) Roles and responsibilities (Redwood / SI / Customer)
12) SLAs and SLOs
13) Pricing summary and optional add‑ons
14) Next steps and pilot handshake
15) Appendix: SOC2 + legal pointers

Objection handling (short scripts)
----------------------------------
- “We’re worried about vendor lock‑in.”
  - Script: Redwood supports model versioning and exportable prompt/eval artifacts; customers can pin model versions and route traffic to alternative variants. Integration uses standard REST/SDK patterns.
- “We need predictable unit costs.”
  - Script: Use Dedicated with commit + overage modeling; share a 90‑day usage projection and run the cost worksheet collaboratively.
